title: Observability weekly notes - 2026-05-25
content:
Observability weekly notes — 2026-05-25

High-level summary:
- Focus this week: tracing sampling rollout, dashboard refresh performance, and initial cost-telemetry batching experiments.
- Canary of adaptive sampling is live in us-west-2 and serving ~12% of traffic. Early signal: 18% reduction in span volume without noticeable loss in error signal for backend services.
- Cost telemetry proto batching reduced ingestion cost estimate by ~9% in the test tenant; still validating across more services.

Key metrics (week-over-week):
- Trace span volume: -15% overall (adaptive sampling + span dedupe).
- P95 trace ingestion latency: 320ms -> 280ms (improved by pipeline batching and retry tuning).
- Dashboard load 95th percentile: 1.1s -> 0.9s after optimizing query materialization.
- Cost (ingestion + storage) per 1M spans estimated: $18.50 -> $16.85 (preliminary).

Tracing
- Work completed:
  - Adaptive sampling canary deployed (PR #212). Sampling policy now considers error status and request path weight.
  - Added tag-based fallback to ensure critical endpoints (payment, auth) are always sampled at 100% regardless of global policy.
  - Improved span deduplication heuristics to collapse identical client and server spans emitted by older SDK versions.
- Observations:
  - Error rate capture for canary looks stable; no missed SLO alerts in canary group for the last 48 hours.
  - Some endpoints with high fanout (search) still generate many child spans even after sampling; follow-up needed.
- Next steps:
  - Expand canary to 35% by 2026-06-01 if current metrics remain steady (owner: Tom Brooks).
  - Implement a cheap pre-aggregation for high-fanout endpoints to reduce child-span pressure (owner: Riley Chen, ETA: 2 sprints).

Dashboards
- Work completed:
  - Dashboard query materialization for high-cardinality panels shipped to staging.
  - New cost dashboard published: "Cost by telemetry type" (link below).
- Issues/bugs:
  - Dashboard refresh occasionally fails when backing query hits >10k groups; workaround added to limit grouping in UI.
  - Users reported stale traces in timeline view when switching time ranges quickly — likely UI caching edge case.
- Next steps:
  - Tune materialization TTLs and add a progress indicator for long-running panels (owner: Miguel Santos, ETA: 1 week).
  - Add a lightweight explorer view for traces to reduce reliance on heavy dashboard panels (owner: Priya Kapoor, ETA: 3 weeks).

Cost telemetry
- Experiment status:
  - Batching + dedupe proto pipeline tested on internal test tenant. Ingestion cost down ~9%, CPU on ingestion nodes down ~12%.
  - Snapshot retention policy draft prepared; suggested move: 30 days hot, 90 days warm (owner: Lena Zhao).
- Risks:
  - Longer batching windows could marginally increase latency for near-real-time alerts. Need to quantify impact on SLOs.
- Next steps:
  - Run a 2-week A/B across two production namespaces to verify cost reduction vs alert latency impact (owner: Lena Zhao; start: 2026-05-28).

Standup / meeting notes (this week)
- 2026-05-25 Observability weekly sync (Attendees: Lena, Tom, Riley, Miguel, Priya):
  - Tom: adaptive sampling canary metrics look good; will propose expansion next week.
  - Riley: working on pre-agg design for high-fanout endpoints; raised question about compatibility with older SDKs.
  - Miguel: dashboard materialization rolled to staging; saw 30% lower query cost in staging cluster.
  - Priya: UI caching bug being debugged; low-priority but affects trace timeline UX.
  - Action: confirm sampling telemetry dashboards reflect per-endpoint coverage (owner: Tom, due: 2026-05-27).

- 2026-05-23 Tracing triage (Attendees: Riley, Tom, ops oncall):
  - Incident OBS-4321 recap: high span volume from a canary client due to misconfigured SDK. Postmortem draft linked in Confluence.
  - Mitigation: temporary rule added to drop spans from that client and notify the app team.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Expand adaptive sampling canary to 35% if no regression (Tom Brooks / 2026-06-01).
- Design pre-aggregation for high-fanout endpoints (Riley Chen / 2026-06-09).
- Tune materialization TTLs + add progress indicator in UI (Miguel Santos / 2026-06-01).
- Start A/B for batching pipeline in two namespaces (Lena Zhao / 2026-05-28).
- Fix timeline caching bug in UI (Priya Kapoor / 2026-05-30).
- Postmortem for OBS-4321 to be finalized and linked (owner: oncall; due: 2026-05-29).

Blockers / open questions:
- How aggressive can we make batching windows before alert latency breach? Need quantification from SLO team.
- Should we add per-tenant sampling overrides in the control plane or keep policy centralized? (ops/SG: trade-offs re: complexity).
- Long-tail cost: do we need a hard cap per-tenant or better alerts + billing cadence?

Links / artifacts:
- Tracing roadmap (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Tracing+Roadmap
- Dashboard: Cost by telemetry type (internal link pinned in dashboard list)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/212
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-4321 (incident), JIRA-OBS-4330 (dashboard materialization)
